sentences.text: Heard Sri Ch. Srinivas, learned counsel for the Petitioners, Ms. Marella Radha, learned counsel for Respondent No.2 and Ms. K. Priyanka Lakshmi, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor representing the State.
3. Learned counsel for the Petitioners would submit that the Petitioners herein are Accused Nos.1 and 2 and the de-facto complainant/Respondent No.2 is the cousin sister of A1.

Learned counsel further would submit that both families have decided to perform the marriage of A3, who is the son of A1 and A2 with the daughter of Respondent No.2 and fixed the date of marriage as 25.06.2019 and engagement was held on 25.01.2019.

Learned counsel further would submit that it is alleged against the Petitioners that after the engagement ceremony, the Petitioners herein demanded unreasonable desires i.e., for 10 acres of land as dowry, for which the accused did not accept and rejected the marriage.
(a) Learned counsel further would submit that the proposal of marriage between A3 and the daughter of Respondent No.2 has been cancelled at the instance of Respondent No.2.
After 2 years of the engagement, the present case has been lodged for the offence U/s 420 IPC.
Both are relatives.

::3::
(b) Learned counsel further would submit that after the engagement A1 as well as the daughter of Respondent No.2 went back to USA for their employment.
Now the son of Petitioners i.e., A3 got engaged with another woman for marriage.
Only to destruct the same, the present case has been lodged.

(c) Learned counsel finally would submit that even as per the allegations made in the complaint are taken into consideration as gospel truth, no offence is made out prima facie much less for the offence punishable U/s 420 IPC.
Learned counsel prays for quashment of the case against the Petitioners.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for Respondent No.2 would submit that at the time of engagement the Petitioners did not open up their mind and after the engagement they have demanded to give 10 acres of land as dowry.

As Respondent No.2 could not oblige their demand for such huge dowry,
they have cancelled the marriage.
Family of Respondent No.2 has been waiting all these days for a change in the mind set of the Accused for performing her daughter s marriage with the son of Petitioners.
(a) Learned counsel further would submit that the Petitioners wanted to perform the marriage of their son with another girl having engaged with the daughter of Respondent No.2.

sentences.text: (b) Learned counsel further would submit that it is a clear case of cheating and accordingly prays for dismissal of the petition.
5. Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor supported the version of the Respondent No.2.

6. Having heard the submissions on behalf of both parties, now the point that would emerge for determination is whether the case against the Petitioners/A1 and A2 is liable to be quashed ?
7.

Judicial conscience of the court should permit it to quash the criminal proceedings while exercising jurisdiction under Section 482 of Cr. P.C. A three-Judge Bench of the Hon'ble Apex Court in MadhavraoJiwajiraoScindia v. SambhajiraoChandrojiraoAngre1 held as follows;

"The legal position is well settled that when a prosecution at the initial stage is asked to be quashed, the test to be applied by the court is as to whether the uncontroverted allegations as made prima facie establish the offence.

It is also for the court to take into consideration any special features which appear in a particular case to consider whether it is expedient and in the interest of justice to permit a prosecution to continue.

This is so on the basis that the court cannot be utilised for any oblique purpose and where in the opinion of the court chances of an ultimate conviction are bleak and, therefore, no useful purpose is likely to be served by allowing a criminal prosecution to continue, the court may while taking into consideration the special facts of a case also quash the proceeding even though it may be at a preliminary stage."

(emphasis supplied) (1988) 1 SCC 692 ::5::
8. As can be seen from the record, the crime has been registered against the Petitioners and their son for the offence punishable U/s 420 r/w 34 IPC on 05.10.2021.
Admittedly, the engagement of the son of the Petitioners with the daughter of the Respondent No.2 took place on 25.01.2019.

It is an undisputed fact that the Petitioners family is not a new family to the family of Respondent No.2,
since Respondent No.2 and Petitioner No.1 are cousins.

A fair look at the contents of the complaint,
the complainant himself stated that the proposal of the marriage has come from the family of the Petitioners and they made it very clear that they do not want any dowry, due to which in the presence of relatives, engagement ceremony took place in the temple of their village on 25.01.2019,
by fixing the date of marriage as 25.06.2019.Such being the case, now the family of the Respondent No.2 is alleging against the Petitioners that after the engagement the Petitioners started unlawful demand of dowry.
9. Simply because the words cheating, deception are used the complaint, it does not become a case of cheating unless it is shown that such an intention is present since inception

Coming to the present case, it is not the case of Respondent No.2 that they have given any amount to the Petitioners or the Petitioners have demanded any amount as Dowry prior to entering the engagement ceremony with the daughter of Respondent No.2.
That apart, the date of engaged was on 25.01.2019.

It is also the case of the Respondent No.2 that the date of marriage has been fixed as ::6::

3 25.06.2019.

sentences.text: Such being the case, the silence on the part of the Respondent No.2 till the date of giving the present complaint.
Admittedly, on 05.10.2021 having received the information that this boy is going to engage with another girl lodging this complaint would speak that it is not a case of cheating.
It appears only to trouble the family of the Petitioners the present case has been lodged.
Absolutely there are no ingredients to attract the offence of cheating in the present case.
In that view, the petition is liable to be allowed.

10. In the result, the Criminal Petition is allowed and the proceedings in C.C.No.133/2023 on the file of Additional Junior Civil Judge, Bapatla, registered for the offences Under Section 420 r/w 34 IPC against the Petitioners/A1 and A2 are hereby quashed.
As a sequel, interlocutory applications if any pending, shall stand closed.
JUSTICE VENKATA JYOTHIRMAI PRATAPA Dt: 12.11.2024 krk ::7
